I've been working this land in Quzhou for over forty years — since I was a young man following my father behind the ox. Back then we grew millet and sorghum. Now it's wheat and corn. That's what this land does, that's what everyone around me grows, and I know these crops like I know my own hands.

I have about 5 mu. My two sons are in the city, so I work it myself and sometimes my wife helps. At my age, I don't want trouble — no new crops, no experiments. Wheat in winter, corn after the wheat is cut. That's my plan, same as last year, same as the year before.

For the wheat, I'll ask at the village supply shop which improved seed they have this year. I don't read the bags myself, but the shop owner tells me what to buy, and it's usually the same kind as my neighbors use. I'll hire the village tractor to do rotary tillage before I sow in October. I always put compound fertilizer down at planting and then add urea in spring when the plants start to grow tall. I water before the ground freezes, again in spring jointing, and once more when the heads come out. Three times is usually enough unless the spring is very dry. I spray once for weeds and once in April if I see disease or aphids.

After the wheat harvest in June, I plant corn immediately — can't waste days at that age. I leave the stubble and plant straight in — no need to till, saves my back, saves money. Hybrid corn seed is what everyone uses now. The yield is better. I fertilize at planting and again when the corn is waist-high. Summer brings rain here, but I'll water once if July is dry. I watch for corn borer and spray if I see the damage.

I don't expect to get rich. I expect to feed ourselves and sell what's left. That's enough.
